Joe Wilder was born in Pennsylvania on February 22, 1922, and he was raised in Philadelphia. His classmates at the Mastbaum School of Music were Buddy DeFranco and Red Rodney. His trumpet playing has been heard with Les Hite, Lionel Hampton, Jimmy Lunceford and Count Basie, as well as in the pit orchestras of New York and he has been called on to perform in the New York Philharmonic and the Smithsonian Jazz Repertory Orchestra. He is a highly respected musician for his skill in ensembles and for his personal jazz phrasing.
His most recent album is entitled “No Greater Love.”
Joe was interviewed by Monk Rowe at the Sarasota Jazz Festival on April 12,
We are filming today for the Hamilton College Jazz Archive. My name is Monk Rowe, and I’m very pleased to have Joe Wilder with us. Thank you very much for coming.
Oh, thank you for inviting me, Monk. I’m sorry you had to track me down.
Well you had such a busy schedule here I feel like I should talk real fast.
Not from my own doing, unfortunately.
Yes. In fact, it seems like your life is busier than ever.
It seems to be and I’d rather that it weren’t actually. But it’s okay, I can’t complain.
